written: 2026-10-26 ~22:00, before any episode on a test split
rule: This is the single look at the reserved test sets (lessons file, item 15). Nothing about the bot, the policies, the judges or the setups changes after these runs; anything that looks wrong is written down, not tuned.
controllers: find_ball: no-memory searchers (perfect recognition, true pose/layout): all hiders, occluder only
set_lamp: the done-at-once floor (episodes needing no press)
episodes: k=0 of each task on every listed config; same episodes for every controller
metrics: task counts (wrong pads, presses needed/extra, find_ball by hider)
inference latency per tick, labelled under load with uptime
breakdowns: go_and_return by target colour (appearances-test: yellow renders ochre)
predictions_before_running: appearances-test: the bot's cyan window starts at 160 deg and test buttons are drawn at 161-167 deg, close to the green/cyan edge after rendering: some buttons may be seen as green pads or missed -> set_lamp press-needed episodes drop most

appearances-test: test mats have saturation 0.15-0.25, above the bot's mat limit of 0.15: the bot will rarely see its mat and will home on odometry alone -> more 'just off the mat' go_and_return failures
appearances-test: dark test yellows render ochre (M1 review) -> yellow targets in go_and_return may be missed or confused with red
arrangements-test: free-standing partitions and centre occluders are new shapes for exploration and hiding; the bot's frontier exploration should cope, find_ball partition hides may be harder
instances-test and distractor-test: close to the corresponding dev numbers (both families were used in tuning, so their dev numbers are development numbers)
the oracle is appearance-blind: its reserved numbers should match its training numbers except arrangements

amendments.written: 2026-10-26 23:30, before any policy episode on a test split (bot/oracle/searcher runs in progress; none of their results seen)
amendments.change: Policy episode cost (up to 1,200 ticks at ~20-30 ms per tick for failures) makes two full policy grids too long for one night. The DAgger policy (the final learned mind) gets the full grid (5 sets x 120 configs x 3 tasks). The BC policy gets the first 40 configs of each set (600 episodes), the same episodes the other controllers ran, so the comparison is paired on those configs.
amendments.also: Policy metric added: tick of the first 'done' (early-done errors). M5 change made on train data only, before this: BC v2 trains on 128-tick windows (v1's 64 never spanned the opening scan) and live frames take the recorder's 128->96->64 path (results/m5/tuning.jsonl).
